subject: MSA redlines: security exhibit & inspection triggers — proposed playbook
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@staginghealth.com
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA redlines: security exhibit & inspection triggers — proposed playbook

Team — forwarding the StagingHealth order-form review queue. Key asks from the customer relate to the security exhibit (SOC 2 access, pen test language, and the scope/evidence cadence). I attached a quick redline (redline_MSA_v3.pdf) with our starting positions — nothing final yet. High-level we should aim for:

- Clear (and narrow) inspection rights so we can avoid broad "on-site" access language. Prefer: SOC 2 attestations + on-demand scoped evidence via shared drive + 30-day notice for any inspection.
- Pen test: limit to non-production with ephemeral accounts, 10 business days' notice, read-only staging where possible, and an ops blackout window to avoid outages.
- Evidence cadence: propose quarterly evidence snapshots (key artifacts) and annual SOC 2 report upload; use shared folder and a single tracking doc for evidence items.

Asks: Laura/legal — can you review the attached PDF and carve a defensible inspection carveout? Karthik — any commercial constraints (credits / SLA) we should be prepared to discuss if they push on evidence timelines? Marissa — please keep the AE loop for timing sensitivity.

I'll draft a short summary email we can send to their security and contracts teams after legal signs off.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Manager, Trust & GTM
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redline_MSA_v3.pdf (PDF, 230KB)]

From: Megan Torres <security@staginghealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Liu <contracts@staginghealth.com>
Date: Sun, 23 Aug 2026 10:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines: security exhibit & inspection triggers — proposed playbook

Hi Tessa — thanks for the heads-up and the redline. A few initial points from our side:

1) SOC 2: we require access to auditor evidence for the last 12 months (any attachments or reports). We prefer a clause that allows us to request the SOC 2 Type II report and supporting evidence on an annual basis.
2) Pen test: we can accept non-prod only, but need a 14-calendar-day notice so our security ops can coordinate. Also: we need remediation SLAs documented — if a high or critical issue is found, we need confirmation that remediation will be prioritized and estimated timelines provided.
3) Evidence cadence: a quarterly snapshot is fine but, for compliance, we also need the option to request ad-hoc evidence up to twice/year with business justification.

I attached our sample addendum for language (StagingHealth_Sec_Addendum_v1.docx).

Are you available Tue morning for a 30-min sync so we can talk through sample sets and what "evidence" will look like?

-Megan
Director, InfoSec — StagingHealth
[Attachment: StagingHealth_Sec_Addendum_v1.docx (DOCX, 48KB)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Megan Torres <security@staginghealth.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2026 15:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines: security exhibit & inspection triggers — proposed playbook

Megan / team — thanks for the constructive addendum. We reviewed both the customer's sample and our internal constraints. High-level counter-proposal (tracked in attached PDF):

- SOC 2: agree to provide the SOC 2 Type II report annually. For auditor evidence, we will provide a scoped bundle limited to assertions relevant to the service (no PII tenant-level logs). We'll surface control mappings for the last 12 months upon execution of an NDA and scoped request.

- Inspection / audit rights: propose "bounded inspection" language: customer may request inspection limited to a predefined set of artifacts and for a maximum of two inspections per 12-month period unless exceptional circumstances are documented. Any on-site access must be mutually agreed and requires 30 calendar days' notice.

- Pen test: we can accept non-production testing with 10 business days' notice (compromise on your 14-day ask). We require written scope and rules of engagement at least 5 business days prior to the start. For remediation, we will commit to a triage timeline: acknowledge within 48 hours, remediate critical/high within 30 days or provide a written exception plan.

- Evidence cadence: propose quarterly snapshots for a short list of operational artifacts (configuration screenshots, patch records, SOC mappings) and annual full-report upload. Ad-hoc evidence requests limited to two per year with business justification and subject to redaction and privacy review. Delivery via our shared drive (linkable folder) and a single evidence-tracking spreadsheet.

- SLA / credits: if evidence delivery is late by >15 business days without prior agreement, customer may request a one-time credit; we prefer to handle operational impacts with prioritized channels rather than automatic financial credits.

I attached our redline PDF (MSA_redlines_for_StagingHealth_20260823.pdf) showing exact language. If you're good with this compromise, Tessa — we can share a short summary email and propose a Tue 10am PT bridge to finalize scope and sample sets.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: MSA_redlines_for_StagingHealth_20260823.pdf (PDF, 96KB)]

From: Tom Liu <contracts@staginghealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Megan Torres <security@staginghealth.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines: security exhibit & inspection triggers — proposed playbook

Laura / Tessa — appreciate the detailed counter-proposal. Tom here from StagingHealth legal. We’re largely aligned with the bounded inspection approach and the pen-test compromise. Two quick clarifications before we confirm:

1) Sample sets: can you confirm whether the quarterly snapshots will include configuration exports (yes/no) and whether tenant identifiers will be redacted?
2) Evidence access logistics: we prefer a one-way SFTP or a read-only folder with time-limited links rather than shared Drive editing. Can Redwood support SFTP delivery or signed time-limited URLs?

If you can confirm those two points we’ll sign-off and book the Tue sync you suggested.

Thanks — Tom
Senior Counsel, Contracts — StagingHealth
